security_audit.summary: Most static matches are Markdown formatting, placeholders, or benign documentation examples rather than executable backticks or exposed credentials. Confirmed risks include unverified remote installer execution, broad organization-scoped credential sharing, private Claude session access, and predictable temporary log files. Static review was capped at 400/477 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 77 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: Remote installer content is executed without integrity verification.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer a verified package manager. Otherwise download a pinned release, verify its signature or digest, show the source, and execute it only after separate approval.

remediation.issue: Private Claude session records can become source material for deployed agents.
remediation.suggestion: Request explicit transcript access, redact secrets and personal data, show the extracted material, and require approval before writing or deploying agent files.

remediation.issue: Credential guidance defaults to organization-wide scope.
remediation.suggestion: Default secrets to the narrowest agent scope. Use organization scope only after confirming every attached agent needs the same credential and permissions.

remediation.issue: Test logs use a predictable shared temporary path.
remediation.suggestion: Create a unique temporary file with restrictive permissions, avoid following symlinks, redact sensitive log fields, and delete the file after testing.

content.value_statement: Building and operating Valet agents requires coordinated CLI, credential, connector, channel, and deployment steps. This skill guides those workflows with explicit confirmation, validation, and testing.
actual_capabilities: Creates, links, deploys, inspects, scales, and removes Valet agents.
Configures organization-scoped and agent-scoped connectors, channels, and environment variables.
Guides catalog selection and custom MCP or command connector setup.
Designs SOUL.md, channel instructions, AGENTS.md, and valet.yaml project files.
Validates connector authentication with Valet-managed secret injection.
Converts a confirmed workflow or Claude session into a reusable agent project.
limitations: Requires the Valet CLI and an authenticated Valet account for account operations.
Cannot obtain third-party credentials or complete external OAuth setup without user participation.
Destructive actions and installation require explicit user approval.
Commands and catalog entries can change, so current CLI help remains authoritative.

use_cases.title: Deploy a Team Agent
use_cases.description: Create an agent, attach shared connectors and channels, configure secrets, deploy it, and verify the complete workflow.

use_cases.title: Build an Event Automation
use_cases.description: Design a webhook, Slack, cron, or heartbeat agent with scoped channel instructions and tested connector access.

use_cases.title: Capture a Repeatable Workflow
use_cases.description: Transform a reviewed working session into reusable agent instructions, setup documentation, and deployment metadata.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect My Valet Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether Valet is installed and authenticated. Then list my organizations and agents without making changes.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Valet agent named <agent-name> in <organization>. Present the file and deployment plan before making changes.

prompt_templates.title: Configure an Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Add a <service> connector and <channel-type> channel to <agent-name>. Prefer catalog resources and explain required credentials without requesting their values.

prompt_templates.title: Design and Validate an Automation
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an agent for <workflow>. Include triggers, scope boundaries, failure handling, least-privilege credentials, deployment steps, connector tests, and end-to-end validation.

output_examples.input: Create a GitHub pull request assistant for the engineering organization.
output_examples.output: A confirmed plan covering the agent project, GitHub connector, webhook channel, required token scopes, deployment, and pull request test.

output_examples.input: My agent needs a different API credential from other organization agents.
output_examples.output: An agent-scoped secret override plan that preserves the shared connector and limits credential exposure.

output_examples.input: Capture this working session as a reusable agent.
output: A session summary with detected tools, corrections, and workflow phases.
A confirmation step before private session details become agent files.
A reusable project with redacted placeholders and setup documentation.

best_practices: Review every command and target organization before execution.
Use least-privilege secrets and test each protected connector before deployment.
Validate manifests and complete an end-to-end channel test before declaring success.
anti_patterns: Do not place real credentials in prompts, project files, examples, or command history.
Do not run installation, destructive operations, or production test events without explicit approval.
Do not share organization-wide credentials when an agent-scoped credential is sufficient.

faq.question: What is required before using this skill?
faq.answer: You need the Valet CLI. Account operations also require an authenticated Valet account.

faq.question: Can the skill install the Valet CLI?
faq.answer: Yes, but it must explain the installer and receive explicit permission before running it.

faq.question: Will the skill ask me to paste API keys?
faq.answer: No. It directs you to set secrets in your terminal and waits for confirmation.

faq.question: Can it configure connectors and channels?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks Valet catalogs first, reuses existing resources, and creates custom resources only when needed.

faq.question: Can it build an agent from a previous session?
faq.answer: Yes. Review and redact the extracted session summary before any generated project is deployed.

faq.question: Does it confirm destructive operations?
faq.answer: Yes. Agent, connector, channel, organization, and session removal require explicit user confirmation.
